news.title: Cape Verde World Cup hero Vozinha has 28m followers, new club and Ballon d’Or nomination but now wants hi
news.lede: Six months ago, Vozinha was a goalkeeper playing in Portugal's second tier, living quietly in the small city of Chaves with little attention beyond Cape Verde. Then came seven saves against Spain at the World Cup, a million Instagram followers in a day and a level of fame he never expected. Now, with more than 28 million followers, he says he would choose his old life back.Seven saves against Spain changed Vozinha's lifeFor anyone who follows football, Vozinha is now one of the recognisable faces of Cape Verde's remarkable World Cup story.

news.title: Europe’s top-flight clubs to get share of £185m from Club World Cup
news.lede: Europe dividing money 50-50 with rest of the world. Confirmation expected after Fifa meeting in October. Europe’s top-flight clubs will share half of the $250m (£185m) solidarity pot from the Club World Cup last year, ending a saga that had caused widespread frustration among those who did not participate in the tournament. Fifa and European Football Clubs (EFC) are close to an agreement that would bring a 50-50 split between sides in Europe and the rest of the world.

news.title: Data shows England made inroads against Spain but they must be more clinical | Andrew Beasley
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel’s side had 36 touches in the Spain penalty area at Wembley but were given a lesson in taking chances. England dominated Spain to an extent very few teams have in recent years. Sadly for them, not in terms of goals. But ownership of the ball is less important than where on the pitch it occurs.

news.title: College football just found the perfect home for Norway’s viral World Cup Viking Row
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, months later, the chant has officially made its way onto American college football fields. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium. In the stands, the student section sat shoulder-to-shoulder in rows, pulling imaginary oars in unison and mimicking the exaggerated motion Norwegian supporters made famous this past summer.

news.title: Retired Soccer Stars Are Cashing In — Beckham’s $51M Payout Tops World Cup Prize
news.lede: Spain's World Cup triumph came with a $50 million prize from FIFA. David Beckham, who retired from professional soccer in 2013, recently collected a business payout worth roughly $51 million. The comparison isn't quite apples-to-apples, but it makes for one heck of a reminder of what retired soccer stars can build after their playing days are over. Retired Soccer Stars Are Turning Fame Into Fortunes Beckham's DRJB Holdings reported almost £50 million ($67 million) in pre-tax profit for 2025, up about 47%, while revenue climbed from £72.2 million to £84 million.

news.title: Spain's Eight Crowns: Football Dominance from Senior to Youth Teams
news.lede: Following the women's Under-20 World Cup triumph in Poland on Sunday, Spain now boasts eight crowns across its men's, women's, boys', and girls' teams. Eight prestigious titles to defend in the coming seasons. Here's the full list, starting with the trophy that kicked off this remarkable run. We begin, of course, with the recently conquered men's World Cup, which completed a historic double alongside their 2024 European Championship success.

news.title: Ghana's Black Challenge drawn in Group D for 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup
news.lede: Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have been drawn in Group D of the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup, where they will face Angola, Colombia and Iraq in the global championship in Mexico. The tournament is scheduled for 13–22 November 2026 in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, and will bring together 24 national teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas. The Group D draw brings together teams from three continents and sets up a significant test for the reigning African champions. Ghana will meet fellow African representatives Angola, alongside Colombia from South America and Iraq from Asia.

news.title: Konsa and O'Reilly doubts to face Czech Republic
news.lede: Konsa and O'Reilly helped England reach the semi-finals of the 2026 World Cup. Ezri Konsa and Nico O'Reilly are both doubts to play in England's Nations League match against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night. The pair were the only two members of the England squad to miss training on Monday morning, with the players following their own individual programmes. Both played the full 90 minutes in England's 3-2 loss to Spain on Saturday.
